The Lagos State Government has urged residents to take precautionary measures against possible extreme heat conditions as the El Niño climate pattern strengthens and the state transitions into the dry season.
The Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Tokunbo Wahab, gave the advisory in a post on his official X handle on Sunday warning that Lagos’ dense population, rapid urbanisation and limited green spaces could worsen the effects of rising temperatures.
Wahab explained that the state’s densely built-up neighbourhoods and extensive road networks could intensify the urban heat effect, making conditions more challenging for residents.
He warned that the anticipated weather conditions could increase heat discomfort, dehydration, respiratory challenges and poor air quality, particularly among vulnerable groups, including children, older persons, pregnant women and outdoor workers.
The commissioner urged residents, community leaders, market associations, schools, business owners and employers to take the advisory seriously, prioritising access to clean drinking water, shaded spaces and proper ventilation.
He also advised residents to stay hydrated, avoid prolonged exposure to direct sunlight, wear light clothing, limit strenuous outdoor activities during the hottest hours and desist from open burning of refuse.

“Beyond immediate precautions, we must confront the environmental factors that worsen urban heat. Protect our trees, plant more, preserve our green spaces, dispose of waste responsibly and desist from activities that degrade our environment,” he said.
Wahab stressed that protecting Lagos from the effects of extreme heat required collective responsibility from government, households, businesses and communities.
He assured residents that the government would continue to strengthen public awareness and collaborate with relevant agencies and stakeholders to improve preparedness and response.
“Let us act early, look out for one another and take collective responsibility for building a cooler, healthier and more climate-resilient Lagos,” the commissioner added.
